newsitem.title: USA: Major stock movements overnight - April 29.
newsitem.headline: Major stock movements overnight - April 29.

text.p: NEW YORK - Wall Street stocks held to moderate gains in mid-afternoon, led by a strong performance by financial stocks.

The Dow industrials were up 26 points at 6765 at 7.30 a.m. NZT. Gainers held a narrow 12-11 edge over declining issues. The Phildelphia Stock Exchange's bank index .BKX was up 13 points, or 2.3 percent, to 567 as big money center banks staged a solid rally.
The Nasdaq Composite rose seven points to 1217 and the S&P 500 gained eight to 773.

LONDON - The UK's FTSE 100 index finished at the day's best levels on Monday, underpinned by a firm gilts market and boosted in the last half-hour of trade by a sharp turnaround on Wall Street. The leading index ended 20 points higher at 4,389.7, despite suffering a weaker opening and relatively quiet trade on caution ahead of the UK election on Thursday.

FRANKFURT - German shares treaded water for most of bourse trade on Monday, but the DAX share index ended lower as support from a stronger dollar was outweighed by investor scepticism about the viability of further gains.
A lower close on Wall Street on Friday evening also helped tip the balance against German shares.
The DAX index ended down 14.21 points, or 0.33 percent, at 3,363.06 points amid poor volumes. In post-bourse trade the DAX stood at 3,372.96 up 15.39 points.

PARIS - French stocks finished higher on Monday, bolstered by polls showing the ruling coalition set to win an upcoming parliamentary election and a stronger dollar. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 13.99 points, or 0.55 percent, at 2,550.25, while the CAC-40 April futures contract rose 17 points to 2,562.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended higher after a quiet day with investors largely on the sidelines ahead of various U.S. economic data later in the week. Sentiment was generally good against the backdrop of a firming U.S. dollar and the favourable interest rate environment, one dealer said.
The Blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 21.0 points, or 0.44 percent, to 4,793.3 points, after touching 4,801.8.
All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended at 3,037.56 points, up 13.32 points, or 0.44 percent, from Friday's close.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed mixed on Monday in extremely light trading as Sunday's Group of Seven (G7) meeting failed to provide fresh incentives to the stock market, and most participants were unwilling to move actively before a holiday tomorrow. The key 225-share Nikkei average closed up 57.51 points or 0.31 percent at 18,670.37, after hovering within a limited range throughout the session.
HONG KONG - Late profit-taking in Hong Kong's hot red-chip sector and caution ahead of this week's heavy calendar of U.S. economic data dragged share prices to a lower close on Monday.
The Hang Seng Index closed down 35.59 points, or 0.28 percent, at 12,610.17. Turnover was HK$13.91 billion, with the focus mainly on China plays, versus HK$15.15 billion on Friday.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market closed lower on Monday, trailing softer U.S. markets lower in a day of light, choppy trade. Trade was generally quiet, with the local market playing catchup to two days of Wall Street weakness after the ANZAC day holiday weekend. Turnover figures were inflated by A$773 million of pre-opening trades related to April series options exercises.
The All Ordinaries index ended 13.0 points lower at 2,461.7.
JOHANNESBURG - South African markets were closed today for a public holiday.
